events.title: Battle of Tippecanoe
events.description: Forces led by Indiana Territory Governor William Henry Harrison clashed with followers of the Shawnee leader Tenskwatawa, brother of Tecumseh, near present-day Battle Ground, Indiana.
events.significance: The battle shook Tecumseh's effort to build a pan-Indian confederacy. It also made Harrison a national hero, and that fame helped carry him to the presidency three decades later.

events.title: Colorado Grants Women the Vote
events.description: Colorado voters approved an amendment to the state constitution giving women the right to vote. It was the first U.S. state to do so by popular vote.
events.significance: The result gave the women's suffrage movement a major early victory and added momentum to the campaign that ended with the 19th Amendment.

events.title: Jeannette Rankin Elected to Congress
events.description: Montana voter Jeannette Rankin won a seat in the U.S. House of Representatives. She became the first woman elected to the U.S. Congress.
events.significance: Rankin broke a barrier in American politics. She did so four years before women nationwide gained the right to vote.

events.title: The October Revolution Begins
events.description: Bolshevik forces seized key points in Petrograd and overthrew the Russian Provisional Government. The date is 7 November on the Gregorian calendar, though Russia's Julian calendar then called it 25 October.
events.significance: The uprising led to the creation of the Soviet state. It reshaped global politics for most of the 20th century.

events.title: Marie Curie Wins a Second Nobel Prize
events.description: Marie Curie was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for her discovery of polonium and radium. She was the first person to win two Nobel Prizes.
events.significance: Curie's achievement remains a landmark for women in science. It showed how far her work on radioactivity had advanced.
